newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-HINGIS CHARGES ON AT WIMBLEDON.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS CHARGES ON AT WIMBLEDON.

text.p: Top seed Martina Hingis's charge toward a second grand slam title gathered momentum when she brushed past Sabine Appelmans of Belgium in straight sets for her first quarter-final berth at Wimbledon on Tuesday.
Hingis, who became the youngest grand slam champion this century when she won the Australian Open earlier this year, has not dropped a set here and took just over an hour to beat Appelmans 6-1 6-3.

The 16-year-old from Switzerland converted her first match point with a deft drop volley just as the first drops of rain fell, but officials were relieved as the dark clouds blew away and play was halted for barely half an hour.
Hingis said afterwards she was conscious she had two further doubles matches to play on Tuesday due to the busy schedule brought on by rain interruptions in the first week.

"I told her (Appelmans) after the match, 'Well I've got two more matches to go, so I want to keep it short' , that's why I played so well," said Hingis, who lost her first match of the year in the French Open final last month.
Appelmans, ranked 19th in the world, dismissed suggestions that such comments bordered on arrogance.
"She's the number one player in the world," she said. "I think, without that attitude, maybe she wouldn't get so far."
Hingis has a favourable draw and next faces Venezuela's Maria Alejandra Vento or Denisa Chladkova of the Czech Republic, both unseeded.

Hingis, who lost to eventual champion Steffi Graf in the fourth round here last year, took only 27 minutes to clinch the first set against Appelmans, dictating terms from the baseline to race to 5-0 lead before the Belgian managed to hold serve.
The 25-year-old, sensing Hingis's reluctance to serve and volley, took the initiative early in the second set by rushing to the net, trying to intimidate her younger rival.
Hingis wildly tried to pass Appelmans with brute force but failed to land the ball in the court, handing her a 2-0 advantage.

The young Swiss regained her composure, however, tempering the aggression and aimed instead for accuracy, breaking Applemans to love in the third game and then levelling at 2-2. She then broke her opponent again in the seventh and ninth games to seal her 41st win of the year.
Eighth seed Aranxta Sanchez Vicario, runner-up here the last two years, breezed through what should have been a tough duel with ninth seeded Frenchwoman Mary Pierce.
The energetic Spaniard, who makes up for her lack of height by her speed about the court, outplayed the stately Pierce 6-1 6-3 in 57 minutes.
Sanchez Vicario had lost her last four matches against Pierce, but on Tuesday she let nothing through and capitalised on the Frenchwoman's frequent mistakes.
Pierce, winner of the Italian Open and a finalist at three other tournaments this year, looked listless and out of touch.

She won the first game but offered the following six to the Spaniard with a flurry of errors. Some powerful shots from the baseline allowed her to get back into the match briefly, but her accuracy was always suspect and Sanchez Vicario won the last eight points of the encounter.
Yayuk Basuki, ranked 26 in the world, became Indonesia's first ever women's singles quarter-finalist at Wimbledon when she accounted for veteran Canadian Patricia Hy-Boulais in straight sets.
